title: Hypothesis-driven model shelf prioritization and competitive gap action plan for regulated verticals
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: produce a repeatable, hypothesis-driven playbook to prioritize which open-model variants and commercial providers should be surfaced in the Redwood model catalog for regulated verticals (finance, healthcare, government). The playbook will combine competitive signals, legal/regulatory constraints, and product fit hypotheses to generate a ranked 'model shelf' and a set of mitigation actions for gaps (e.g., fine-tuning needs, red-team evals, certifying KMS integrations).

Scope: focus on model quality dimensions relevant to regulated customers: hallucination rates on domain Q&A, PII leakage probability, instruction-following in constrained policy contexts, latency/cost trade-offs for privacy-preserving deployment modes (Private/VPC). Exclude multimodal models for this tranche.

Deliverables: (1) scoring rubric (quantitative weights + signal sources), (2) prioritized model shelf CSV + rationale for top 10 candidates, (3) gap action plan mapping each gap to an owner and ETA, (4) dashboard prototype that surfaces top signals and historical deltas, (5) PRD for next-phase onboarding experiments.

Scoring rubric (draft): must-link signals to testable hypotheses:
- Safety/Hallucination score (35%): measured by domain-specific evals and red-team testsets.
- Data residency/PII risk (25%): static analysis + known pretraining provenance signals.
- Latency/cost fit for private deployments (15%): bench benchmarks from First-Party tests.
- Functional accuracy on vertical tasks (15%): closed-book retrieval QA, slot-filling.
- Community/support & license risk (10%): OSS license clarity, community adoption signals.

Primary data sources: internal eval harness (Eval-Lab), customer logs (anonymized), open-source crawler metrics, partner due-diligence writeups. Expected signal refresh cadence: weekly for bench results, monthly for provenance/legal findings.

Hypotheses (examples):
H1: Models with higher provenance-clarity and lower third-party data footprints reduce regulatory friction for mid-market finance customers by 30% (measured via onboarding time).
H2: A modestly quantized 8-bit variant with specialized safety fine-tuning will meet policy thresholds while reducing private deployment cost by ~22%.

Experiment plan: run safety evals and latency bench on a seeded set of 25 candidate models -> produce normalized scores -> conduct two blinded manual reviews (PM + Research) for top 8 -> pilot onboarding for 2 models into a dedicated pilot customer sandbox.

Acceptance criteria: scoring rubric documented and approved by PM + Legal; prioritized CSV accepted by Solutions Engineering; dashboard prototype functional; action plan has owners and ETA <= 8 weeks for critical gaps.

risks: - Bench infra quotas (ENG-32901) could delay scoring runs; - Legal provenance checks may disqualify high-performing models late in process; - Limited labeled vertical eval data may inflate false confidence. Mitigations: request quota bump, run parallel manual provenance triage, reweight uncertainty in rubric.
